plan: In a second-price auction, bidding your true value is a dominant strategy regardless of the number of competitors or their strategies, since you pay the second-highest bid, not your own bid. Overbidding risks paying more than the item is worth if you win, while underbidding risks losing profitable opportunities. Therefore, the optimal strategy is to bid exactly my private value of $10, ensuring I maximize expected profit without unnecessary risk.

This is a second-price sealed-bid auction (Vickrey auction). The dominant strategy in a second-price auction is to bid exactly my true value, regardless of what others do. Bidding my value ensures I win whenever it's profitable (my value exceeds the second-highest bid) and lose when it wouldn't be profitable. Overbidding risks paying more than my value if I win against a bid between my value and my bid. Underbidding risks losing profitable opportunities. Therefore, I will bid my true value of $30.

This is a second-price sealed-bid auction (highest bidder wins, pays second-highest bid). In such auctions, bidding your true value is the dominant strategy regardless of other bidders' behavior—since I only pay the second-highest bid if I win, overbidding risks paying more than my value, and underbidding risks losing profitable opportunities. With no prior history to adjust for, truthful bidding maximizes expected profit. My value is $25, so I will bid exactly that.
